t109_start_p1: You might go looking for your little one and get mad instead, or realize you’ve been staring at the rug. I count that as pl/ork too, even if it feels like it’s in the way. Before you decide where it’s coming from, ask it what it’s trying to stop, or what it wants. You can tell that part something like, “I see you. I’m not going to force my way past you. What’s going on?” Or however you’d actually say that. Then wait and listen patiently.
t109_start_p2: Maybe it just has something to say. It could be your little one, mad that you took so long to come back, or a part of you that’s trying to protect you. Maybe it’s that parent you inherited, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each. I wouldn’t spend long deciding what to call each part, though. Every part of you learns from how the others treat it, your little one included. A part of you that’s trying to protect you might warn you about something, and when you hear it out, it doesn’t have to get any louder.
t109_start_p4: If nothing comes, that’s fine for now. No need to answer for that part just because you’d set this up as a healing session. Even without the answer, you can notice what sets the reaction off, and you can understand what the reaction is propelling you toward, and away from.
t109_hardest_p1: Then there’s the stuff that’s hardest to tell anyone, and of course that’s exactly what you need help with. Maybe it’s an urge that scares you, or something you did that could get you in legal trouble. I’d assume that what you tell won’t be completely confidential, especially if it sounds like something dangerous. Just don’t hold back a danger that’s happening now from people who can help, and get anyone in danger safe before worrying about the rest. Sometimes telling on yourself is the thing that keeps someone safe, whatever it costs you legally.

t109_sec_hardest:
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
Then there’s the stuff that’s hardest to tell anyone, and of course that’s exactly what you need help with. Maybe it’s an urge that scares you, or something you did that could get you in legal trouble. I’d assume that what you tell won’t be completely confidential, especially if it sounds like something dangerous. Just don’t hold back a danger that’s happening now from people who can help, and get anyone in danger safe before worrying about the rest. Sometimes telling on yourself is the thing that keeps someone safe, whatever it costs you legally.
You know that DM you deleted? It can still be sitting on their phone as a screenshot 🙈, and whatever’s on a company’s server can get handed over if a court asks. Just because Mr. Boopaloopa was your name on WhatsApp doesn’t guarantee you’re anonymous, by the way.
And some of the people you’d tell, like therapists, teachers, and doctors, can be required to report certain things (a few laws cover everybody, too). Which things depends on where you live, and it’s nowhere near every crime you might mention. The cops are hopefully the obvious ones to be careful with, even if they pretend to care.
So I’d ask them, before handing over any tricky specifics: “What does the law require you to report?” That’s a normal and expected question. Although personally I wouldn’t even bother with that, because whatever they tell you today, the law can change tomorrow.
You can always rephrase things as a dream narrative to get the emotional content across without triggering alarm bells (although I actually got in trouble with TalkSpace therapy bot even for a dream!).
